Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Sudden severe left-sided throbbing headache starting around mid-day today.
  - Preceded by visual “zig-zag” lines and blurred vision; photophobia (wearing sunglasses). No clear trigger identified.
  - Nausea with two episodes of vomiting.
  - Headache worsens with leaning forward and with head/neck movement; non-migratory.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset today at mid-day; a few hours in duration at time of consult.
  - Prior similar episode a few weeks ago, lasting a couple of days.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): 
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: Not reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: Not reported.
  - Drooling: Not reported.
  - Nasal symptoms: Not reported.
  - Ocular symptoms: Visual aura (zig-zag lines), blurred vision, photophobia.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: Not reported.
  - Dyspnea: Denies breathlessness.
  - Swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): Not reported.
  - Ear symptoms: Not reported.
  - Neck symptoms: Headache worsens with head/neck movement; no explicit neck pain reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - Similar headache a few weeks ago; lasted ~2 days; managed with unspecified painkillers and rest. No ED visits/hospitalization; no injection therapy documented.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: Not documented.
  - Current medication: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive), for contraception, started ~3 months ago (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Prior/acute treatments: “Painkillers” previously (not specified). Today advised to use paracetamol or co-codamol, and NSAIDs (ibuprofen or naproxen); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Lives alone. Works in the fashion industry; reports high job stress. Non-smoker; no alcohol use. No routine exercise.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: Denies breathlessness; no stridor reported.
- Mental status and associated features: Not recorded.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Probable migraine with aura.
  - Justification: Unilateral throbbing headache, preceded by visual aura (zig-zag lines), associated blurred vision and photophobia, nausea/vomiting; prior similar episode weeks ago; no focal neurological deficits (no speech issues, weakness, numbness, balance problems), no fever, no head injury.
- Serious intracranial pathology (e.g., meningitis, brain tumor) considered less likely based on current history; patient reassured by clinician.
- Conflict noted: Clinician referenced “some disease, like Lyme’s” prior to headache onset; this was not corroborated by the patient.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Analgesia: Paracetamol or co-codamol; NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Keep a headache diary to identify potential triggers.
- Specific instructions provided to patient:
  - If symptoms are not improving in the “next two three days,” or if worsening, “come back and see me straight away.”
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Worsening headache, lack of response to medications, worsening neck pain, any new limb weakness, or vision changes—seek urgent reassessment (“come back and see me straight away”).
- Follow-up:
  - Follow-up next week to review symptoms and consider prophylactic migraine therapy if headaches persist.
  - No ENT/allergy referrals discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions (verbatim if provided):
  - “come back and see me straight away.”

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergy list not documented.
  - Vitals and full physical/neurological examination (including fundoscopic exam) not recorded.
  - ENT examination (ears, nose, throat) not documented.
  - Analgesic/NSAID dose, route, frequency not documented.
  - Review of medication contraindications (e.g., combined oral contraceptive use in migraine with aura) not documented.
  - Pregnancy status not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Clinician mentioned “some disease, like Lyme’s” before headache onset; not confirmed by patient.
- Transcript quality:
  - Occasional incomplete/overlapped statements; one unclear clinician reference (Lyme’s). Otherwise understandable.
